subject: Issue with crs when fitting LGCP

messages.author: 0047b623f2d48d40
messages.subject: Issue with crs when fitting LGCP
parts:
Hi there, 

I'm getting an error about crs not matching when I run my lgcp model with NDVI as a covariate:

> fit6 <- lgcp(+   components = cmp6,+   data = spatial_list$nests,+   samplers = spatial_list$transects,+   domain = list(+     coordinates = spatial_list$mesh,+     distance = INLA::inla.mesh.1d(seq(0, W, length.out = 30))+   ),+   formula = form6,+   options = list(bru_initial = list(lsig = 2),+                  bru_verbose=4)+ )

Error in sp::over(where, data) : identicalCRS(x, y) is not TRUE

As I have run this model with a covariate for forest for example, I assumed it was the crs of the NDVI layer that was proving the issue. However:

> st_crs(Covariates$NDVI) == st_crs(spatial_list$mesh)
[1] FALSE

> st_crs(Covariates$Forest) == st_crs(spatial_list$mesh)
[1] FALSE

> st_crs(Covariates$NDVI) == st_crs(Covariates$Forest)
[1] TRUE

> spatial_list$mesh$crs
Coordinate Reference System:Deprecated Proj.4 representation: +proj=tmerc +lat_0=0 +lon_0=-15 +k=0.9996 +x_0=500000 +y_0=0 +datum=WGS84 +units=km +no_defs

NDVI
Coordinate Reference System (CRS) arguments: +proj=tmerc +lat_0=0 +lon_0=-15 +k=0.9996 +x_0=500000 +y_0=0 +datum=WGS84 +units=km+no_defs

Do you have any idea what the issue might be here? 
Thank you!

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Issue with crs when fitting LGCP
parts:
Hi,
as we're in the middle of some major updates in the mesh and crs
handling related code, please state precisely what package versions
you have (the full sessionInfo() output can be helpful).
In particular, if you have inlabru 2.8.0, please install the
development version (you can install both that and the required
fmesher package from r-universe, see the package github.io pages) and
try again to see if it's an issue that's already been fixed.
(Or if you already have the development versions, there might be a new bug...)

From the crs output, it's not clear if you have modern crs objects;
they would usually show something about "WKT" information, which is
what is really used internally by sp and sf, so the old proj4
representations don't tell the whole story.
What's the output of fm_crs(spatial_list$mesh) and fm_crs(Covariates$NDVI) ?

Finn

Hi,
as we're in the middle of some major updates in the mesh and crs
handling related code, please state precisely what package versions
you have (the full sessionInfo() output can be helpful).
In particular, if you have inlabru 2.8.0, please install the
development version (you can install both that and the required
fmesher package from r-universe, see the package github.io pages) and
try again to see if it's an issue that's already been fixed.
(Or if you already have the development versions, there might be a new bug...)

From the crs output, it's not clear if you have modern crs objects;
they would usually show something about "WKT" information, which is
what is really used internally by sp and sf, so the old proj4
representations don't tell the whole story.
What's the output of fm_crs(spatial_list$mesh) and fm_crs(Covariates$NDVI) ?

Finn

ips <- fm_int(domain = list(coordinates = spatial_list$mesh, distance

= INLA::inla.mesh.1d(seq(0, W, length.out = 30))),
samplers = spatial_list$transects)

You had "corrected" it by adding a ")" in the wrong place. ;)

Finn

Is this with updated fmesher or the one you already had?
In either case, it looks very strange, as it doesn't show any
coordinates for ips, and also no line info for the transects, but it
still associates what looks to be identical crs'es to them.

I'll need the str(ips) output.
Also,

sf::st_as_sf(ips)
sf::st_as_sf(spatial_list$transects)

Finn

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Issue with crs when fitting LGCP
parts:
You have been using fmesher indirectly via the devel version of
inlabru, and the upcoming INLA build will also use fmesher directly.

There's some more info here that will apply to the new INLA version
https://inlabru-org.github.io/fmesher/articles/inla_conversion.html

It's designed to work the same as the old functions for now, but allow
new features to be added.

The crs related code has been in inlabru for a while, including the
current CRAN version, but the functions were already called fm_* in
anticipation of being moved to the new package.

I can't really see what's wrong with your code; I'd need to run it on
my own system to step through to the error; if you're able to share
the data and code needed to trigger the error that would be great (by
private email).
But I suspect that a useful fix for you would be to convert the whole
thing to sf objects instead of sp. Only some minor changes needed
apart from a bunch of sf::st_as_sf() on all your data objects (and
convert any SpatialPixels/Grid variables to terra::rast() instead).
Instead of comp(coordinates, ...) and domain=list(coordinates = mesh),
you'll need comp(geometry, ...) and domain=list(geometry = mesh).

Several of the inlabru website Articles have been updated to use sf
instead of sp, so have a look around the github.io website for
inlabru.

Finn

Hi Finn, 

Thanks for this, I've convert my data and covariates as suggested.

Tried running the below code but giving me an error:

#### SPDE Only Model ####
# Specify hazard-rate detection function
hn <- function(distance, lsig) {1 - exp(-(distance / (exp(lsig)))^-1)}

# Define a (Matern) covariance function for the SPDE
matern <- inla.spde2.pcmatern(spatial_list$mesh,
                              prior.sigma = c(1, 0.01),
                              prior.range = c(10, 0.9))

# Specify components of model
cmp <- ~ mySPDE(main = geometry, model = matern) + lsig(1) + Intercept(1)

# Specify formula
form <- coordinates + distance ~ mySPDE +
  log(hn(distance, lsig)) +
  Intercept + log(2)

# Fit model with only SPDE
fit <- lgcp(
  components = cmp,
  data = spatial_list$nests,
  samplers = spatial_list$transects,
  domain = list(
    geometry = spatial_list$mesh,

distance = INLA::inla.mesh.1d(seq(0, W, length.out = 30))
  ),
formula = form,
options = list(bru_initial = list(lsig = 2),

bru_verbose=4)
)

  `sp` input detected but no `coordinates` domain present.

Do I need to amend coordinates in "form" too?

You have been using fmesher indirectly via the devel version of
inlabru, and the upcoming INLA build will also use fmesher directly.

There's some more info here that will apply to the new INLA version
https://inlabru-org.github.io/fmesher/articles/inla_conversion.html

It's designed to work the same as the old functions for now, but allow
new features to be added.

The crs related code has been in inlabru for a while, including the
current CRAN version, but the functions were already called fm_* in
anticipation of being moved to the new package.

I can't really see what's wrong with your code; I'd need to run it on
my own system to step through to the error; if you're able to share
the data and code needed to trigger the error that would be great (by
private email).
But I suspect that a useful fix for you would be to convert the whole
thing to sf objects instead of sp. Only some minor changes needed
apart from a bunch of sf::st_as_sf() on all your data objects (and
convert any SpatialPixels/Grid variables to terra::rast() instead).
Instead of comp(coordinates, ...) and domain=list(coordinates = mesh),
you'll need comp(geometry, ...) and domain=list(geometry = mesh).

Several of the inlabru website Articles have been updated to use sf
instead of sp, so have a look around the github.io website for
inlabru.

Finn
